title.en: Quadratic equations: factorisation, completing the square and formula

text.en: A rectangular garden is 3 m longer than it is wide, and its area is 28 square metres. What are its sides? Writing x(x + 3) = 28 gives a quadratic equation.

A quadratic equation is ax squared + bx + c = 0 with a not equal to 0. Its solutions are called roots.
Method 1, factorisation: split the middle term and use that if pq = 0 then p = 0 or q = 0.
Method 2, completing the square: write x squared + (b/a)x as a perfect square plus a number, then take square roots.
Method 3, formula: x = [-b plus or minus the square root of (b squared - 4ac)] divided by 2a.
The expression b squared - 4ac is the discriminant, written delta.
If delta is positive there are two different real roots; if delta = 0 there are two equal real roots; if delta is negative there are no real roots.
The sum of the roots is -b/a and the product of the roots is c/a.

problem.en: Solve x squared - 5x + 6 = 0, then use the formula on 2x squared + 3x - 2 = 0.

text.en: Factorise: x squared - 5x + 6 = (x - 2)(x - 3) = 0, so x = 2 or x = 3.

why.en: Numbers with sum -5 and product 6 are -2 and -3.

text.en: For 2x squared + 3x - 2: a = 2, b = 3, c = -2, delta = 9 + 16 = 25.
x = (-3 plus or minus 5)/4, so x = 1/2 or x = -2.

prompt.en: List the three methods of solving a quadratic and what the discriminant tells us.

requiredIdeas.en: Positive, zero, negative give two, equal, no real roots

commonMisconceptions.en: Forgetting the sign when b is negative

points.en: Quadratic: ax squared + bx + c = 0, a not zero.
Roots by factorisation, completing the square or the formula.
delta = b squared - 4ac decides the nature of the roots.
